edit.explain.motion: Two identical elliptical gears each turn about one focus, with the foci 80 mm apart (the major axis length). The contact point always lies on the line of centres and runs 40 mm each way along it, so the two radii to it trade length while their sum stays the same, and the speed ratio is their quotient. As the driver turns steadily, the driven gear turns the other way, speeding up and slowing down once per turn, from a third of the input speed to three times it: in the 120° of input around the meeting of the long radius with the short one it turns 240°.
edit.ratio.typical: ratio swings between (1-e)/(1+e) and (1+e)/(1-e) each turn; 1/3 to 3 at e = 0.5
edit.build.range: input 360° continuous; output 360° per input turn, the other way, speed varying from 1/3 to 3 times the input
edit.build.notes: Mesh with the long radius of one gear against the short radius of the other. Solve contact with r1 + r2 = cd. Space teeth equally by arc length along the pitch curve, not by angle: 20 teeth on a perimeter of 234.8 mm, module about 3.74. Any tooth count works for identical ellipses because both gears complete a turn together. At e = 0.5 the pitch curve's normal tilts up to 30° from the radius, so the teeth must be generated by rolling the two pitch curves (conjugate), not set as rack teeth on the normal.

claims.text: it rolls backwards by one lobe, 40°, for every input turn
the output turns once, backwards, per 9 input turns (9:1)

edit.explain.motion: The input shaft carries an eccentric that makes the cycloidal disc wobble around inside a ring of 10 fixed pins. Because the disc has 9 lobes, one fewer than the pins, it rolls backwards by one lobe, 40°, for every input turn, so the output turns once, backwards, per 9 input turns (9:1). Pins on the output flange run in holes in the disc whose radius exceeds the pin's by the eccentricity: each hole circles its pin, so the wobble is left behind and only the slow turn reaches the flange.

edit.build.defining_relations: ratio i = n/(N - n) = 9, output opposite to input; disc profile (t from 0 to 2 pi): x = R cos t - Rr cos(t + psi) - e cos(N t), y = -R sin t + Rr sin(t + psi) + e sin(N t), psi = atan2(sin((1-N)t), R/(e N) - cos((1-N)t)); e < R/N, here eN/R = 0.8 and the lobes are 2e = 8 mm deep; the disc's rolling circle (radius e n = 36) rolls inside the pins' (radius e N = 40), touching on the line O-E; disc angle = -th_in/n relative to ground, disc centre at e on input angle; output angle = disc angle (the pins and holes form parallelograms O, E, hole, pin).
edit.build.notes: N = 10, n = 9, R = 50, pin radius 5, e = 4: no undercut (the trochoid's smallest convex radius of curvature is 12.8 mm) and no pin interference over the cycle. Trace a point on the disc's rolling circle (radius 36): it draws ten cusps per output turn, one at each pin. One disc is drawn so its lobes read; a real unit balances it with a second disc 180° out of phase. The disc sits on top of the pins, the output flange underneath.

edit.explain.forces: Contact is mostly sliding along the thread, so friction is high and efficiency falls from about 90% at low ratios to under 50% at high ratios. The drive locks when the lead angle is below the friction angle: here the lead angle is 5.7°, and at rest steel on bronze has a friction coefficient of about 0.12 (friction angle about 7.3°), so the wheel cannot turn the worm. Running, the coefficient falls to about 0.06 (3.7°), which is why the lock is not reliable under vibration.
edit.build.defining_relations: ratio i = z2/z1 = 30; lead L = z1 pi m; tan(gamma) = z1/q; a = m(q+z2)/2; efficiency (worm driving) = (cos an - mu tan g)/(cos an + mu cot g) approx tan g / tan(g + phi); self-locking (the wheel cannot drive) when gamma < phi, phi = atan(mu / cos alpha): at rest mu about 0.12 gives phi 7.28° > gamma 5.71°, so it locks; running mu 0.06 gives 3.65°, below gamma.
edit.build.notes: Show the worm thread as a helix advancing one axial pitch per turn while the wheel turns one tooth. The default view is the auxiliary view down the worm's axis; a section on the wheel's mid-plane shows the thread profile moving like a rack. Show a lock icon if the wheel is driven.

claims.text: each wave generator turn shifts the flexspline back by two teeth, 24°
the flexspline turns once, backwards, per 15 input turns (15:1)

edit.explain.motion: An elliptical cam with a thin ball bearing (the wave generator) spins inside a flexible cup with 30 external teeth (the flexspline), bending it into an oval so its teeth engage a rigid 32-tooth ring at the two ends of the long axis and stand clear at the ends of the short one. Each wave generator turn shifts the flexspline back by two teeth relative to the ring, 24°, so the flexspline turns once, backwards, per 15 input turns (15:1). With the finer 100 and 102 teeth of the other tooth set the reduction is 50:1, but the bend is then too small to see.
